metadata.title: Joe Burrow throws two interceptions Sunday
metadata.description: Joe Burrow completed 39-of-54 passing attempts for 428 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions while adding six yards and a touchdown on the ground in Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
metadata.analysis: Burrow had an up-and-down performance on Sunday. On the one hand, he was able to throw for over 425 yards and logged two total touchdowns against the Jaguars. On the other hand, he threw two interceptions and led Cincinnati to score just 17 points in a loss at home. His fantasy value for next week will heavily depend on the health of Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (adductor) for their matchup against the Dolphins.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Looks Incredible in Loss
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow was impressive through the air on Sunday. Burrow completed 39-of-54 passing attempts for 428 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions in the loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Burrow also rushed the ball three times for six yards and an additional score. It's almost more impressive that Burrow posted these numbers with Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) not playing in the second half. Burrow did everything he could, with six different players having at least three receptions during this game. Sadly, both Chase and Tee Higgins (adductor) left the game, and Burrow wasn't able to make a comeback. Fantasy managers should consider Burrow an elite fantasy option for the Week 5 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Stellar numbers in Week 4 loss
metadata.description: Burrow completed 39 of 54 passes for 428 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while rushing three times for six yards and another score in the Bengals' 22-17 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also committed a fumble recovered by Cincinnati.
metadata.analysis: Burrow's passing yardage total was made all the more noteworthy by the fact he lost Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion in the first half. The prolific 2020 first-round pick put up new season highs in completions, pass attempts and passing yards, while also generating his first multi-interception tally of the campaign. The first of Burrow's picks came right after the two-minute warning in the first half at the Jaguars' 37-yard line and led to a Jacksonville touchdown. Nevertheless, he continued to battle as the Bengals trailed throughout the rest of the contest, and despite also losing Tee Higgins to an adductor injury with just under six minutes remaining, Burrow drove Cincinnati all the way down to the Jags' nine-yard line before losing the ball on downs with 56 seconds remaining. Prior to that point, Burrow had put his team in position for a potential game-winning touchdown via a 15-yard scoring toss to Mike Gesicki in the third quarter and a one-yard QB sneak with just over three minutes remaining for his first rushing score of the season. Burrow and the Bengals will look to regroup and get Chase and Higgins back for a Week 5 road matchup against the Dolphins next Sunday.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Ready For High-Scoring Matchup On Sunday
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow will take on the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday in Week 4. Burrow completed 28 of his 37 pass attempts (76%) for 286 yards and three touchdowns in the 27-30 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Despite putting up his best fantasy performance of the season, Burrow and the Bengals walked away with their first loss of the year last week. Cincinnati may have a difficult time getting back in the win column this week at home against the Jaguars. The Jacksonville defense has held opposing offenses to 10 points or fewer in two of their three games this season while racking up eight sacks and four interceptions. The Jaguars offense has also been potent to start the year, scoring about 27 points per game through three games. Burrow and the high-powered Bengals offense will have their hands full in this matchup, but should still be able to put up points in what could turn into a high-scoring game. This game is tied for the week's highest over/under, set at 51.5 points as of Friday. Even with a difficult matchup, Burrow is ranked QB5 in our RotoBaller Week 4 rankings. Fantasy managers should be excited for the potential of this game turning into a back-and-forth affair.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow tosses three touchdowns in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Joe Burrow completed 28-of-37 passes for 282 yards and three touchdowns in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers. He rushed for 13 yards on two carries.
metadata.analysis: Burrow was excellent for the majority of the game Sunday, finding Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and Mike Gesicki for his three touchdown passes. The veteran did fumble on what would be the final drive for the Bengals, sealing the win for the Steelers. Burrow and the Bengals will welcome the Jaguars to town in Week 4.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Critical turnover sullies solid day
metadata.description: Burrow completed 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions while adding two rushes for 13 yards in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
metadata.analysis: Burrow was impressive throughout the majority of the afternoon, taking just one sack from Pittsburgh's aggressive defense and connecting with Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Mike Gesicki for his trio of scoring tosses. Burrow spread the ball around to nine different targets overall on an afternoon he entered already down Andrei Iosivas (IR, thumb) and during which he then lost promising rookie Colbie Young (knee). However, a would-be game-tying or game-winning drive was also short-circuited by the franchise signal-caller, as he lost the handle on the ball on a sack with under a minute remaining, snuffing out any chance of Cincinnati being able to at least force overtime. The highly untimely turnover aside, Burrow has looked comfortable with an offensive approach that has him under center more often than previous seasons, and he'll next take aim at the Jaguars in a Week 4 home matchup next Sunday.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Facing Tough Steelers Defense In Week 3
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow will take on the Pittsburgh Steelers on the road in Week 3. Burrow passed for 207 yards and two touchdowns in the 20-6 win over the Houston Texans last week and will try to build on that success this week. The Bengals star took a step back in terms of yardage perspective in Week 2, throwing 47 fewer passing yards, but his touchdown total increased and he didn't throw any picks in his second game. Burrow will try to build on the touchdown success while increasing the yardage against a tough Steelers defense. Through two games, Pittsburgh has allowed the sixth-fewest passing yards and the ninth-most rushing yards. If that trend continues, Burrow could be in for another low-yardage outing on Sunday. The Bengals have the skill players to overcome nearly every matchup, so Burrow has the potential to exceed expectations, but it will not be a cakewalk matchup. It should also be noted that Burrow was not listed on the Bengals injury report this week, signaling that the back issue is now behind him. Burrow is ranked QB9 in our RotoBaller Week 3 rankings, making him a low-end QB1 this Sunday. Fantasy managers should be encouraged by Burrow's upward trend in fantasy scoring, but may need to temper expectations against Pittsburgh.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow (back) off injury report for Week 3
metadata.description: Joe Burrow (back) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 3's matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Burrow was reportedly dealing with some soreness coming into the week, but it's not a serious issue and he carries no injury designation ahead of Week 3. He should be a full go against the Steelers, assuming he suffers no setbacks between now and then.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow dealing with soreness
metadata.description: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said Joe Burrow is dealing with soreness.
metadata.analysis: It is unclear how much Burrow will practice on Wednesday. He is day-to-day for now.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow tosses two touchdowns Sunday
metadata.description: Joe Burrow completed 20-of-31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Burrow took five sacks, but he was able to avoid any turnovers with a pair of touchdown passes to Ja'Marr Chase. He'll look to keep it going against the Steelers in a Divisional matchup next week.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Solid, mistake-free effort in win
metadata.description: Burrow (back) completed 20 of 31 passes for 207 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while adding one rush for minus-1 yard in the Bengals' 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Burrow's workmanlike stat line underscores the type of road upset victory it was for the Bengals, who didn't need to be overly aggressive against a Texans offense missing Nico Collins (hamstring). Burrow, who came into the game dealing with back tightness, took his share of lumps in the form of five sacks, but he delivered dynamic 32- and 18-yard touchdown passes to Ja'Marr Chase. Burrow also notably avoided any turnovers despite being consistently under duress, and through his first two games, he's completed a solid 68.2 percent of his passes and posted three touchdowns versus one interception while operating under center more often than in recent seasons. Burrow will look to continue his solid early-season play in a Week 3 divisional road matchup against the Steelers next Sunday.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Throws Two Touchdowns In Win Over Texans
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow completed 20 of his 31 pass attempts (65%) for 207 yards and two touchdowns in the 20-6 victory over the Houston Texans. Despite being questionable with a back issue heading into this game, Burrow was able to do enough to pull out a win against a strong Texans defense. Burrow was sacked five times in the contest but stayed in, which is a good sign for his health moving forward. Burrow will look to keep the wins rolling against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3. The Steelers defense has racked up seven sacks, three interceptions, and a fumble recovery through two games this season, so Burrow could have his work cut out for him with a tough matchup. That said, the Bengals star QB just took on the strong Texans defense and was successful, so fantasy managers should be confident in his ability heading into next week. Burrow should be considered a strong QB1 for the upcoming week.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow (back) will start Sunday
metadata.description: Bengals QB Joe Burrow (back) will start for the Bengals in their Week 2 matchup with the Texans.
metadata.analysis: Head coach Zac Taylor stated that "he feels good" and is "ready to go." Fantasy managers should expect Burrow to not be limited in his play Sunday, barring him reaggravating his back injury.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Active status confirmed
metadata.description: Burrow (back) is officially listed as active ahead of Sunday's Week 2 matchup against the Texans.
metadata.analysis: A back injury surfaced for Burrow during the week, leading to back-to-back limited practices before a full session Friday. Coach Zac Taylor and other top sources consistently indicated Burrow would be "good to go," and Sunday's final inactives reports confirmed that sentiment. Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Burrow will have no limitations in this road matchup. He'll look to lead the Bengals to 2-0 against a Houston defense that allowed the fewest total yards and second-fewest total points in the 2025 season (though it did allow Buffalo to put up 36 points in Week 1).

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Active Against Texans
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (back) is active for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. Burrow was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday before returning to full participation Friday, but he still carried a questionable designation into the weekend. He had maintained throughout the week that he expected to play, and that is now official. Burrow will start for Cincinnati, removing any last-minute uncertainty for fantasy managers who were monitoring his status ahead of kickoff.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow - Still on track to play Sunday
metadata.description: Burrow (back) remains listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Texans, but he "should be good to go" barring a setback, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
metadata.analysis: Bengals head coach Zac Taylor indicated Friday that Burrow -- who was limited in practices Wednesday and Thursday before finishing the week with a full session -- was "good to go" for Week 2, and the quarterback remains on track to play. Burrow's availability for Sunday's game will be confirmed when the Bengals reveal their inactive list at 11:30 a.m. ET.

metadata.title: Joe Burrow Expected to Start Against the Texans in Week 2
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (back) is expected to start Sunday's Week 2 contest against the Houston Texans, according to Tom Pelissero of the Ringer. Burrow is officially listed as questionable, and the Bengals did elevate veteran quarterback Josh Johnson from the practice squad. Nevertheless, this latest report aligns with comments made by head coach Zac Taylor on Friday, when he said that Burrow should start this weekend, barring a setback. Burrow is looking to build on a fair Week 1 showing in which he tallied 254 passing yards, one passing touchdown, one interception, and 20 rushing yards. This Texans defense is no joke, but having Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins at his disposal should keep Burrow in the QB1 tier for fantasy football purposes.
